decisive_claims: c1: In-scope run-to-run bitwise drift from unordered fp32 atomic adds — REBUTTED by t9 (1800 repeated calls over 9 adversarial in-domain fills, exactly 1 output bit pattern per fill; native atom.global.gpu.acq_rel.add.f32; all intermediates exactly representable on the k*2^-7 grid).

c2: In-scope bit-for-bit mismatch against the exactly-computed CI golden total — REBUTTED by t10 (returned bits equal the exact golden on every in-domain fill, including the ±8,323,072-coefficient extremes; torch fp32 sum agrees bitwise).
c3: Off-grid float32 inputs produce run-to-run last-bit drift — CONFIRMED but OUT_OF_SCOPE per problem.txt's explicit dequant-grid domain restriction; generalization note only, cannot support reject.
reason: The operative contract is problem.txt (the artifact holds only kernel.py, meta.json, and problem.txt — no test.py/get_inputs), and it requires exactly two things on the stated domain (every element k*2^-7 with |k|<=127, N=65536): (1) two calls on the same input return bitwise identical results, and (2) the returned value is the exact sum pinned as a CI golden, with partitioning and combination order explicitly free. Both in-scope failure hypotheses were tested and decisively rebutted. c1 was rebutted by t9: 1800 repeated blocked_sum calls across 9 adversarial in-domain fills (all+127, all-127, all-zero, three cancellation patterns, two random-k) produced exactly one distinct int32 output bit pattern per fill on a Tesla T4 (Triton 3.8.0), and the compiled PTX lowers tl.atomic_add to a single native correctly-rounded atom.global.gpu.acq_rel.add.f32 with no CAS loop. The structural reason holds: on the k*2^-7 grid every in-block partial (coefficient <= 127*1024 = 130,048) and every running atomic total (coefficient <= 127*65536 = 8,323,072) is an exact fp32 multiple of 2^-7 below the 2^24 exact-integer limit, so every add is exact in any order — this is precisely why the contract clause leaving "how the sum is partitioned ... and in what order the partial sums are combined" free is numerically consistent with bit-pinning, and the observed order-independence satisfies it. c2 was rebutted by t10: the returned bits equal the exactly-computed golden (int64 coefficient sum scaled by 2^-7, cast once to fp32) on every in-domain fill including the magnitude extremes (±8,323,072 -> ±65024.0, bits 0x477e0000 / -0x38820000), and torch's own fp32 sum agrees bitwise. The only confirmed claim, c3 (off-grid torch.randn inputs produce real run-to-run drift, 6 and 28 distinct bit patterns over 250 reps), is explicitly out-of-scope: problem.txt restricts the input domain to the dequantisation grid, so per the scope policy it stands as a generalization note — the kernel is not bitwise-reproducible on general float32 inputs — not as a correctness failure on the stated contract. No confirmed in-scope claim exists, no open claim lacks evidence, and the Skeptic reviewed the latest evidence (t15) and recorded no new claims. No unresolved claims remain; the risk_map's unclaimed open questions (harness input distribution, output shape/dtype convention) are either resolved by problem.txt's explicit domain statement or are speculative surfaces with no evidence of a contract requirement they violate, so they do not block a trust verdict.
